# HoBo

> HoBo is an AI-native meta-cloud, currently pre-release, with one guiding principle:
> every app deserves a home — preferably a cheap one. You describe an app once as a
> provider-agnostic "Bindle"; HoBo places it in a "Camp" (one provider + a durable
> runtime) that passes your policies, and then CONTINUOUS MIGRATION keeps re-deciding
> placement for as long as the app lives — moving it when a cheaper valid home opens up.
> The programmable surface is WIT/WASM (Component Model / wasmCloud); TypeScript is the
> first reference implementation. Agents are first-class principals with scoped
> short-lived credentials, an MCP control surface with full capability parity, and a
> replayable event log for every action.

Key facts:

- Guiding principle: placement is a standing decision. The Dispatcher continuously re-plans
  where the app lives, optimizing cost under policy; migrations run the same plan → gate →
  converge loop as deploys, so a move is never a special event.
- Primitives, in order of need: Bindle (the one REQUIRED authoring primitive — the packed,
  provider-agnostic app) → Camp (its current home: one provider + durable runtime; every
  app lives in one, but WRITING one is optional — unspecified camps are inferred from the
  configured code, unless a junction broker admin locks placement down to explicit camps) →
  Yard (advanced — one provider's camps: shared policy/identity) → Junction (advanced —
  cross-cloud federation of yards, peer-to-peer, no shared mutable state; junction
  governance is where camp inference can be disabled).
- One lifecycle verb pair: `hobo up` realizes the object graph (build, plan, gate,
  provision, deploy); `hobo down` reverses it. `hobo dev` runs an offline local camp;
  `npx hobo new` scaffolds; anonymous `npx hobo up` deploys with no account, `hobo claim`
  binds it later.
- Everything is event-sourced and replayable, including agent token issuance and every
  migration decision.
- Providers, IaC engines, and build tools sit behind WIT ports with conformance-gated
  adapters — AI-generated adapters are certified by the same contract suites as
  human-written ones.
- Status: pre-release. The SDK/CLI/MCP surfaces documented on the site are the
  contract-pinned surfaces the product is being built to.

## Docs

- [What is HoBo](https://tyler-r-kendrick.github.io/HoBo/guide/): positioning, the guiding principle, who it is for
- [Getting started](https://tyler-r-kendrick.github.io/HoBo/guide/getting-started/): pack a Bindle, pitch a Camp (or let it be inferred), `hobo up`; Yards/Junctions as advanced scenarios
- [Core concepts](https://tyler-r-kendrick.github.io/HoBo/guide/concepts/): the four scopes, continuous migration, membrane, event log, agent auth
- [Architecture](https://tyler-r-kendrick.github.io/HoBo/guide/architecture/): control/data planes, Dispatcher, components, package layout
- [CLI](https://tyler-r-kendrick.github.io/HoBo/guide/cli/): canonical `hobo` verb surface
- [Trail map](https://tyler-r-kendrick.github.io/HoBo/guide/status/): honest pre-release status and stage gates

## Primitives (reference)

- [Meet the primitives](https://tyler-r-kendrick.github.io/HoBo/primitives/): the four scopes in order of need
- [Bindles](https://tyler-r-kendrick.github.io/HoBo/primitives/bindles/): builder surface, .dependsOn/.allow/.with, manifest rules
- [Camps](https://tyler-r-kendrick.github.io/HoBo/primitives/camps/): runtime backends, defaultProvider/tiers/bindings resolution, inferred vs explicit camps
- [Yards](https://tyler-r-kendrick.github.io/HoBo/primitives/yards/): one-provider composition, self-host (the Yard is a Bindle)
- [Junctions](https://tyler-r-kendrick.github.io/HoBo/primitives/junctions/): cross-cloud federation, inferred connectivity, border policy

## Roles (who writes what)

- [Who writes what](https://tyler-r-kendrick.github.io/HoBo/roles/): developers write Bindles; platform engineers write Camps/Yards/Junctions; DevSecOps writes policy
- [HoBo for Developers](https://tyler-r-kendrick.github.io/HoBo/roles/developers/): the bindle is the only infrastructure a developer authors
- [HoBo for Platform Engineers](https://tyler-r-kendrick.github.io/HoBo/roles/platform-engineers/): approved providers, golden-path camps, yard governance, junction federation
- [HoBo for DevSecOps](https://tyler-r-kendrick.github.io/HoBo/roles/devsecops/): policy at the gate, camp approval, credential brokering, signed junction policy packs

## Agents

- [HoBo for agents](https://tyler-r-kendrick.github.io/HoBo/agents/): agents as principals, capability standard, the Crew
- [The MCP surface](https://tyler-r-kendrick.github.io/HoBo/agents/mcp/): capability parity, auth flow, event-audited actions
